To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The average δ13 C value of C3-plants from the modern Gangeti Plain is lower than the observed δ13 C value (~− 27 ‰) of bulk SOM derived from contemporary C4 plants in the middle Siwalik.

(1) δ13C values are lower in modern C3 plants from lower and middle Gangeitc Plain compared to global values and (2) δ13C value in phytolith-occluded carbon is similar with bulk carbon in phytoloths and bulk SOM.

(i) the average δ13C of C3 plants in modern Gangetic Plain, which is lower than globally, is controlled by stomatal regulation; (ii) C4 plants are abundant in the Gangetic Plain and their δ13C values are controlled by leakiness of carbon; (iii) the average δC13 value of occluded carbon of phytoliths is controlled by the source plants and (iv) the OC concentration in phytolith is controlled by the plant species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the modern vegetation dynamics of the Gangetic Plain and the implications for paleovegetational studies.
the δ13C of plants and phytoliths from the Gangetic plain and their implication in paleovegetational and paleoclimate reconstruction.
the δ13C value in modern C3– C4 plants from the middle and lower Gangetic plain, India and its implication to paleovegetation reconstruction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the δ13 C values of C3 and C4 plants are controlled by MAP and the δ13C value for C4 plants are higher compared to C3 plants.
the δ13 C values in C3- and C4-plants and occluded carbon of phytoliths from the modern Gangete Plain, India are controlled by MAP and the δ13C value in SOM is a result of C4 plants contribution.
C4 plants are present in Gangetic Plain at least since the middle Miocene (11 Ma), but the contribution of C4 plants to the SOM pool is not clear.
